subject: Temporary latency tolerance & reduced remedy proposal for Blue Meridian pilot
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie@blue-meridian.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.k@blue-meridian.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLO ask — Blue Meridian (proof-of-concept)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed by the latency profiles. We're ready to move forward with a limited proof-of-concept (pilot) but we need two temporary concessions to make the test meaningful for our production traffic:

- Latency: allow p95 target up to 300ms (currently your standard p95 is 120–150ms). We expect most requests to be under 200ms but want a tolerance for traffic spikes during load testing.
- Remedies: in exchange for a small pilot discount and a purchase commitment if metrics are met, we'd like the standard service credit schedule softened for the first 90 days (lower cap on total credits and a higher threshold before credits kick in).

I've attached a proposed SLO matrix and a short note on expected QPS (blue-meridian-slo-matrix.xlsx).

Our procurement team is also asking for a commercial point person and a short timeline so they can align approvals. Can your side confirm whether this is something you can authorize at the VP/Exec level, or if we need a formal route to Deal Desk / Exec?

Thanks,
Sophie Lane
Head of Integrations, Blue Meridian
Sophie.Lane@blue-meridian.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: blue-meridian-slo-matrix.xlsx
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — Blue Meridian (proof-of-concept)

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Blue Meridian's ask. Highlights: temporary p95 latency tolerance to 300ms for the first 90 days of a pilot and a request to limit financial remedies in that window in exchange for a pilot discount / committed purchase. See attached SLO matrix.

Options I'm proposing for Exec consideration (trade-offs spelled out for Deal Desk):
1) Approve 90-day pilot exception: p95 up to 300ms, cap total service credits to 5% of monthly invoice, offer 15% pilot discount.
2) Conservative: approve a 30-day trial with 99.5% uptime floor and 10% discount; full remedies apply after 30 days.
3) Decline exception — standard SLOs and remedy schedule, no pilot discount.

Timeline: Customer wants to start the pilot week of May 24, so we need a decision this week to get commercial and legal redlines in DocuSign.

Marissa — can you advise commercial appetite? Jonas / Karthik — any immediate legal/ops blockers I should flag?

Best,
Evelyn
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — Blue Meridian (proof-of-concept)

Evelyn — thanks for the summary. I'm sympathetic to doing a pilot with looser latency targets if we can keep commercialization simple and limit downside. High-level commercial stance:

- Pilot discount: we can go up to 15% for a time-boxed pilot (helps win the deal).
- Remedy cap: must be a fixed dollar or percentage cap — prefer percentage to keep calculation simple. Recommend 5% cap for pilot period.
- Duration: 60–90 days is acceptable for a pilot but customer needs to accept that standard SLOs and remedies resume automatically after that window.

I'll defer final approval to Jonas for anything that changes invoice exposure beyond 5% and to Karthik for contract redlines. If Jonas signs off, I'll instruct Deal Desk to prepare the commercial addendum.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — Blue Meridian (proof-of-concept) — legal redlines

Quick notes from legal/commercial review after looking at the SLO matrix and proposed commercial terms:

- We can accept a temporary relaxation of latency p95 to 300ms for a pilot, provided the pilot is explicitly time-boxed and auto-reverts (we should include an automatic revert clause in the exhibit).
- Remedies: agree to a pilot cap at 5% of monthly fees, but require that the cap applies only to remedies against Redwood; exclude indemnity or security breach language from the cap.
- Contract redlines: add explicit pilot exhibit; require customer signoff on the SLO appendix; include a clause that we may terminate pilot early for safety/abuse/perf regressions.
- Operational requirement: we need a named operational contact and an onboarding playbook (JIRA:SUP-9876) included prior to start.

If commercial wants a higher discount (>15%) or a larger cap, we'll need Exec signoff on financial exposure.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — Blue Meridian (proof-of-concept) — exec disposition

Approved with conditions. Rationale: Blue Meridian is strategic in our vertical and a constrained pilot accelerates a larger ARR opportunity; exposure is acceptable within limits. Conditions below must be included in the commercial addendum and executed before pilot start:

- Pilot duration: 90 days.
- Latency: p95 tolerance to 300ms for pilot window only.
- Remedies cap: 5% of monthly fees (absolute cap for remedy payments during pilot).
- Pilot discount: 15% applied to pilot invoices only.
- Auto-revert clause: SLOs and remedies revert to standard terms after pilot automatically.
- Operational pre-reqs: onboarding checklist completed, named ops contact, and SUP-9876 ticket open.
- Exec notification: Finance will be informed if credits approach 3% of monthly fee.

Marissa — please instruct Deal Desk to prepare addendum and send to Blue Meridian via DocuSign. Evelyn — please confirm customer acceptance and ask procurement to sign the SLO exhibit.

Jonas Weber
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
